entities.summary:
Saint Publius, also known as Publius of Malta or Publius of Athens, was an early Christian bishop and saint. He is considered the first Bishop of Malta and one of the first Bishops of Athens.

Born in the 1st century CE, Publius' early life is shrouded in mystery, with some accounts suggesting he was a Roman citizen and others claiming he was of Greek descent. His ascension to the bishopric of Malta is believed to have occurred during the reign of Emperor Trajan (98-117 CE), although the exact date is unknown.

Publius played a significant role in the early Christian church, particularly in the development of the Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom. He also established a number of churches and monasteries throughout the Mediterranean, including one in Athens that became a major center of Christian learning.

The legacy of Saint Publius can be seen in the numerous churches and monasteries he founded, which continue to be revered by Christians today. His feast day, celebrated on December 11, is marked by processions and liturgies in many parts of the world.

Despite the passing of centuries, Publius' impact on the development of Christianity and Western civilization remains a testament to the enduring power of faith and spirituality.

In recent years, archaeological excavations at the site of the ancient church of St. Publius in Malta have uncovered a wealth of artifacts and relics, including a rare 4th-century mosaic that is believed to have been created by Publius himself.

As we reflect on the life and legacy of Saint Publius, we are reminded of the profound impact that individuals can have on the course of human history.
